title: The French Revolution - OverSimplified (Part 1)
beats: Party skit: nobles gossip, royal wedding bedroom scene; seeds 'France is in financial ruin' refrain
France was prosperous for the few; 80% poor; war with Britain lost; debt
Drunk peasant asks 'why do nobles get to be rich?' enacting the Enlightenment
Louis XVI weak, funds American revolution, more debt; Marie Antoinette 'Madame Deficit'
Tax the poor: collectors list each tax in turn, 'there's a tax for that' (windows, tithe, salt, a child's tears)
Summarize why anger grew; natural disaster, bread price, riots
Estates General: one vote per estate; skit 8:34-9:20 shows 2-to-1 outcome
National Assembly, Tennis Court Oath, Jacobins
Fear then anger then violence chain stated as a rule
Bastille storming; king's denial skit ('pike-head deity')
Assembly's choice to applaud violence; some historians say it paved the way
Marat's newspaper; Declaration of Rights (men only)
Women's march to Versailles; 'let them eat cake' rebuked
King agrees to return to Paris; ends with the separation removed

metrics.misconception: partial: 'let them eat cake' shown as out-of-touch not literal (15:34); France as beautiful nation (1:44) undercut
metrics.brute_force: yes 4:50: enumerate taxes one by one so the unfairness is felt before it is named (6:27)
metrics.examples: taxes (5 in a row), estate votes (3 in a row, then 2 outcomes), king denial skit; escalating absurdity
metrics.ending: Part 1 ends on royal family forced to Paris, plus VPN sponsor and pointer to Part 2

new_moves.name: enumerate-until-absurd
new_moves.what: Make a systemic burden felt by escalating itemized examples (taxes), then name it in one sentence

new_moves.name: simulate-the-rule
new_moves.what: Run the institutional rule (one vote per estate) as a tiny vote so viewer sees the outcome

new_moves.name: stated-causal-law
new_moves.what: Compress mood into a transferable rule: fear unchecked becomes anger becomes violence

theory: The strongest move is enumerating one concrete case at a time until the viewer feels the unfairness before the label ('tax inequality') appears. The same device turns an institution (three estates, one vote each) into a rule-run simulation whose outcome the viewer predicts.
velocity: Ghost hands: step through an itemized list with a visible running tally before reveal
Scene builder: voting/rule simulations with learner prediction before outcome
Orchestrator: label causal chain with a 'what could push them over' bridge before each escalation
Evals: reveal summary only after at least 3 enumerated instances
quote: Fear, left unchecked, often boils over into anger.
